checks: All four continuous sets lie in K, so the two prescribed K fibers are exact and the two exposed endpoint fibers are unchanged.

The endpoint and its reflected copy at the other middle base form a centrally symmetric submeasure about the respective mark, disjoint in base from its own K. Any containing closed halfspace captures at least a of the pair and at least q in its own K, including pure-base boundary mass.

At any middle point a minimizing ordinary cap is attained by joint continuity and has a finite tilt isolating the paying endpoint and own fiber. Each endpoint can instead be isolated by outward tilt and has ordinary depth at most a/2.

For an ordinary interior deepest mark every critical plane is proper, so the regular coarea derivative is two-sided with positive section measure. Varying its ordinary normal through the mark forces the section centroid to be the mark. A strictly inward point of the same cap would admit a higher threshold and smaller mass, and a distinct boundary point of depth q would contradict the centroid identity.

The compact active set of ordinary normals balances zero: separation gives a uniform margin increase when moving the mark in the indicated opposite direction, with nonactive normals separated by a positive old mass gap. A positive Carathéodory circuit then precludes another deepest point outside all its caps.

The common tilt bound gives strict full/empty statuses and regularity, and the positive normal relation covers every designated whole base plane. In the strict reflected-core case a positive-volume opposite-middle trace captures positive volume outside the reflected endpoint, violating equality. Its zero-volume trace strictly misses the inner reflected endpoint, so the paying endpoint is strictly inside.
